how: The index moved sideways for the next three months.
S&P 500 −1.0% to 2084.07. It fell 10.4% over the next ten sessions.
It had fallen 2.1% the day before. The selling carried over the weekend.
1,278 trading halts, most in exchange-traded funds. S&P 500 −3.9%; first close 10% below the high. VIX closed at 40.7, its high for the episode.
The index rose 3.9% the next session.
Closing low of the retest was 1881.77 the day before. A 13% rally to early November followed.
The rally of 13.0% in 49 sessions failed; this became the start of the second leg down.
Close 2073.07. The index fell 11.8% over the next eight weeks.
Over 42% of NYSE issues at 52-week lows. The intraday low broke the August low; the close, 1859.33, was just under it.

t: Closing low 1829.08; oil at $26.21; credit peaks
how: Oil, high-yield bonds and the Baa spread (3.63 points) turned the same day. VIX 28.1 against 40.7 in August.

t: Third gain in a row: +1.65%; Nasdaq +2.2%
how: Cited by practitioners as the follow-through day on the Nasdaq, day 4. The index was 5.3% off the low.

t: +2.4%: follow-through day by the study’s rule
how: Session 12 after the low on the S&P 500. Close 1978.35.
Led by small and mid-sized companies, unlike the thrust of October 2015 that failed.

t: Back above the 200-day average; NYSE thrust
how: Session 20, 10.6% above the low. Deemer’s twenty-day breadth signal fired the same day.

t: Fed projections cut from four increases to two
how: S&P 500 +0.6% to 2027.22. The change in guidance came five weeks after the low.
